decisions.reason: As a close-to-core prescription product introduced only in 2024, it still has unresolved upside and can be supported with the firm's existing formulation, production and pharmacy-facing capabilities at relatively low incremental option-holding cost.

Because this generic antidepressant is distant from the firm's established offer, likely more exposed to price-driven reimbursement competition, and requires capabilities and market access less aligned with the firm's strategy, the option value no longer justifies tying up resources versus stronger-fit projects.

This close-to-core combination tablet fits the firm's established prescription portfolio and manufacturing base, and after only one year on the market there is still too much uncertainty to abandon an option that could scale through existing channels.

The bone and joint supplement builds directly on the firm's self-care and differentiated pharmacy product ambitions, and as a relatively low-cost product to maintain it is worth keeping while market acceptance becomes clearer.
